page.notes: The woodcut initial is read as "A", giving "Aquiliana" (the Lex Aquilia-type formula); the first letter is the ornamental capital. The number after LIBRO is printed as a single mark that I read as I; it may be a printer's sign. The "I" in "instituí" and the printed line-end quotation marks are uncertain. The argument text has the printed spellings "instituedi", "familiâs", "mortē", "testamē tum"; these are copied as printed, with the line-end "testamē" joined to "tum" as "testamenti" in my reading. Some words are cramped at the line ends and are read with reasonable but not complete certainty.
